Alice M: quick q — where can I pull TTFT broken down by model + route for prod? trying to tune the p99 alert, but not sure which panels to use or which promql to run.

Bob K: try the latency->TTFT dashboard in Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ttft/ttft-overview?orgId=1&var-env=prod
Key panel is 'TTFT by model/route (p50/p95/p99)'. For adhoc promql:
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_ttft_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, model, route))
```
That gives you p99 TTFT in seconds by model+route over a 5m window.

Carol S: +1 to Bob. If you want a time series for a single route use the panel variable or add `route=~"^/v1/chat"` etc. For tokens/sec (to correlate load) use: 
```
sum(rate(runtime_tokens_generated_total{env="prod",model=~"$model"}[1m])) by (model)
```
That is tokens/sec for the model. Correlate spikes in tokens/sec with TTFT jumps.

Alice M: thanks — is there a recommended way to avoid alert noise from short blips? p99 is pretty jumpy on small routes.

Dave R: yeah — two quick knobs: increase the evaluation window (use 5m->15m) and add `for: 10m` in the alert so it must persist. Also consider using `max_over_time` vs direct histogram_quantile depending on what you want to catch. Example alert snippet: 
```
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_ttft_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[5m])) by (le, model, route)) > 1.5
for: 15m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: https://wiki.redwood.ai/runbooks/ttft-p99
```
If a route has very low QPS (<1r/s) the p99 is meaningless — add a filter to exclude low-traffic routes using `sum(rate(...)) by (route) > 0.1`.

Carol S: also consider alerting on a sustained increase in p95 instead of p99 for higher-sensitivity, or create two tiers: p95 warning (pager: no) and p99 incident (pager: yes).

Bob K: for tracing, when you see a TTFT spike open Jaeger traces: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/search?service=runtime&lookback=1h and filter by trace.tag route/model. Look for cache misses or long first-token kernels.

Alice M: perfect. I'll try the queries now. If I modify the alert YAML I'll open a PR and @Dave R for review. Can someone paste the exact panel link for the per-route heatmap?

Bob K: per-route heatmap: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ttft/ttft-heatmap?orgId=1&var-env=prod&panelId=7 — set `var-interval=5m` and `var-model=All`.

Carol S: add this quick Kibana logs query to grab runtime logs around a trace id: `trace_id: "<trace-id>" AND env: "prod"` and use `@timestamp` +/- 2m.

Dave R: one more tuning tip: if you're tuning the alert threshold, validate against historical SLOs. run this to get 30d p99 baseline per route: 
```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_ttft_seconds_bucket{env="prod"}[30d])) by (le, model, route))
```
Use the baseline as starting threshold (e.g., 2x baseline for paging).

Alice M: ok will do. can someone add a short section to the runbook with these links + promql snippets? I can draft. :thumbsup:
